verdict: Only if you're ready for excise regulation. INACAN pitched India's first cocktail in a can on Shark Tank India Season 1 and got a deal from all five sharks. Ready-to-drink cocktails are growing, but alcohol licensing, state-by-state pricing and advertising bans make this very different from a soft-drink brand.
angle: Young urban drinkers want convenient, lower-alcohol drinks for parties and travel. Each state sets its own excise duties, label approvals and distribution rules, so expanding state by state is slow and costly. Alcohol advertising is banned, so events, bars and word of mouth are your main channels.

faq_extra.q: Can you advertise alcohol in India?
faq_extra.a: No. Direct advertising of alcohol is banned, so brands rely on events, bar partnerships, surrogate products and word of mouth. Plan your marketing around that from the start.
